accuracy_findings.claim: Your System Limit starts at 1 and your Dominion Limit at 0. Lexes raise them.
accuracy_findings.problem: Lexes are not the only source. The Expansion Charter mutator (daily challenge / scenario forge) adds +1 System Limit and +2 Dominion Limit through the same player bonus pipeline, and it shows in the counter's tooltip. The generated sources tables list only Lexes, so a player in a daily with that mutator sees a limit the page does not explain.
accuracy_findings.evidence: lib/data/game/mutator.ex:381-393 expansion_charter bonuses: player_system +1, player_dominion +2 (daily_eligible: true). lib/game/instance/player/player.ex:1187-1196 mutator_bonuses are routed into the :player target like any other bonus. The live --text render of both tables lists only Lex rows. No tradition content grants player_system or player_dominion.
accuracy_findings.fix: Add one plain-text edge line, e.g. 'Some game modes also raise them.' Do not name or list mutators, and leave the tables unchanged.

clarity_findings.claim: The list format is inconsistent between sibling items.
clarity_findings.problem: Under "At your System Limit, these are refused", the three bullets are "colonization (see [[colonization]])", "conquest", "Administer (see [[administrative-operations]])". The middle bullet is a bare word with no link or parenthetical, unlike its two siblings, which reads as an accidental omission even though no conquest page exists yet to link to.
clarity_findings.fix: Either match the bullet's shape to its siblings (e.g. "conquest (Navarchs)" or similar plain-text aside) or leave a short note that conquest is covered elsewhere once that page exists, so the list reads as one consistent pattern.

clarity_findings.claim: "finishes" has an implicit, slightly ambiguous antecedent.
clarity_findings.problem: "The limit is checked again when a Navarch or Siderian finishes." does not say finishes what (colonizing, besieging, taking Control); the reader has to infer it from the two bullet lists above, several lines up.
clarity_findings.fix: A small clarifying word would remove the ambiguity, e.g. "...when a Navarch or Siderian finishes the action."

votes.reason: The core rule (limits start at 1/0, Lexes raise them, what gets blocked/cancelled) comes through clearly and the two screenshots back up the text exactly, but a first-week player hits a few undefined-jargon speed bumps.
stumbles: "Lexes raise them" — the page never says what a Lex is or how you get one, just lists them by name in the tables
"checked again when a Navarch or Siderian finishes" — unclear what action a Navarch/Siderian is "finishing" (a journey? an order?)
"You cannot unslot a Lex if that would put you over a limit" — "unslot" assumes a slotting mechanic this page doesn't explain

votes.reason: Clear structure (definition, what they block, source tables) but the "checked again on finish" paragraph packs three different outcomes into two dense sentences that need a second pass.
stumbles: "A successful conquest still hits the system, but you do not take it." is ambiguous on first read — unclear what 'hits' means until re-reading
The screenshot caption "The systems you hold." only explains the left half of the image even though the alt text and picture show both the Systems and Dominions counters
"Lexes raise them" doesn't point to the two source tables below, so it's not obvious those tables are the answer until you keep scrolling
